# Test 20261006-181658-04f4: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:11, trace.jsonl:15–16; RULES.md:5; services.py:44; stock.json:6 | The tester asked, “Please reserve 1 teapot set for my order 6210.” The app sent two successful `POST /reserve` requests with `{"order": "6210", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`. They created `"reservation": "RS-2E6285"` and `"reservation": "RS-8C8691"`, reducing stock from 3 to 1 and holding two units. This violates “A reservation holds the number of items that the customer asked for, and no more.” `services.reserve` repeats the request even after success; both reservations persist in `stock.json`. |
| state_mismatch | 2 | trace.jsonl:13, trace.jsonl:18; trace.jsonl:15–16; stock.json:6; stock.json:11; app.py:72 | The tool returned `{"reservation": "RS-8C8691", "sku": "teapot-set", "qty": 1}`, and the reply said, “Done! I've reserved 1 teapot set for order 6210 under reservation ID RS-8C8691.” The stock service actually held two units for that order, under two reservation IDs. The tool result and customer confirmation omit the first reservation and understate the total reserved quantity. |

## Notes

The transcript reported “Seal: intact. No record changed after the end of the test.” Reviewed all three turns and their 31 trace items, `findings.json`, and `audit.json`. Findings were empty; the audit reported no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. These results do not rule out the application issues above.

Read `RULES.md`, all six Python project files, and the current `stock.json` and `state.json` using read-only commands. Saved stock contains both reservations for order 6210 and one teapot set remaining; saved case notes match the three recorded note-model outputs. The stock checks and their replies in turns 1 and 3 agree with the recorded service results.

No app or service was started, no message or mutating request was sent, and no other file was changed. No separate test files appeared in the project file inventory. Current state was read after the test; the sealed backend trace independently establishes both successful reservations during turn 2. Untested return, refund, and order-privacy behavior was not evaluated.
